meta.question: How many MICHELIN restaurants are within 1 hour of travel by subway or bus from each candidate hotel?
meta.important_limitation: Las Vegas has NO subway, metro or light rail. The only rail is the privately operated Las Vegas Monorail, which runs on the east side of the Strip from MGM Grand to SAHARA. Public transit is the RTC bus network. So 'subway or bus' was implemented as 'Monorail or RTC bus', and that substitution is stated wherever the result is used.
meta.how_times_were_produced: One published travel time anchors the model: RTC Route 203's own timetable gives 14 minutes from Decatur to Las Vegas Blvd. along Spring Mountain Road. Walking speed, Monorail speed, Deuce speed, platform waits and the transfer penalty are declared planning assumptions printed on the Transit page. The generator in tools/build_matrix.py reproduces every number and can be re-run to sensitivity-test the assumptions.

monorail.uses: Covers the Strip from MGM Grand to SAHARA only. It does NOT reach Chinatown/Spring Mountain Road, the Arts District, Downtown/Fremont Street, ARIA, Bellagio, Wynn/Encore, Resorts World or the Gold Coast.
monorail.holiday_notice_found: The operator publishes modified and early-closure dates. A notice captured during verification listed early closures Nov 29 – Dec 15, 2026. Check the site for the Feb–Mar 2027 window before relying on late-night service.

bus.operator: Regional Transportation Commission of Southern Nevada (RTC)

key_routes.corridor: Las Vegas Boulevard — South Strip Transit Terminal to Downtown / Fremont Street
key_routes.relevance: Serves every Strip hotel in this study. Does not turn west onto Spring Mountain Road.

key_routes.corridor: Runs the length of Spring Mountain Road, the road the Chinatown MICHELIN cluster sits on
key_routes.relevance: This is the route that reaches Chinatown. Its timetable carries a timed stop at Las Vegas Blvd, and the timed run from Decatur to Las Vegas Blvd takes 14 minutes.

key_routes.corridor: Strip and Downtown express; passes are also valid on residential routes
key_routes.relevance: Useful for the Arts District and Downtown cluster.

bus.correction_notice: An earlier version of this page stated that Chinatown had no Deuce and no bus service and was therefore over an hour from every Strip hotel. That was wrong. Route 203 serves Spring Mountain Road directly and its official timetable proves it. Because Chinatown holds 7 of the 24 MICHELIN restaurants, the correction materially changed every hotel's score.
bus.visitor_rule: Visitors pay Strip and All Access fares. Passes are valid on all routes, so a Strip pass also works on Route 203.
bus.children: Children 5 and under ride free with a paying adult.

travel_band_rules.rule: Under about 14 minutes on foot from the hotel entrance, no transit needed.

hotel_transit_profile.note: No Monorail station, but Spring Mountain Road crosses Las Vegas Boulevard at the north end of the property, so Route 203 to the seven-restaurant Chinatown cluster boards about 0.35 mi away. That single geography gives it the highest one-hour count in the study.
Off the Boulevard behind Fashion Show mall, but close to Spring Mountain Road, so Chinatown is reachable. Nothing else is: zero restaurants fall within 30 minutes.

hotel_transit_profile.note: Best combination of Monorail access and cheap rate. Only the three off-Boulevard singles fall outside an hour.
Monorail station at the property plus the Deuce outside, and the cheapest verified rate of any hotel with a station on site.
Two MICHELIN restaurants inside. Unavailable for 15–22 Feb 2027.

hotel_transit_profile.note: Two starred restaurants inside and a Monorail station inside, but the farthest south, so Chinatown and the north Strip cost it time.
Set back behind its lake, which adds walking to every trip.

cluster_geography.note: No Monorail station. Reached on the Deuce, or Monorail to Harrah's / The LINQ plus a walk.

The densest cluster in the city — 29% of the list in about two miles — and it is served by RTC Route 203, not by the Monorail or the Deuce. Route 203's timetable stops at Las Vegas Blvd, so the far north Strip is the best-placed base for it.
Reached on the Deuce / SDX downtown corridor.
About nine miles southwest of the Strip.
